canonical_name: Oscillatory behavior of differential-equation solutions (catalog family label; exact proposition open)
statement_blocker: The catalog fixes no differential equation, order, domain, solution class, coefficient or endpoint assumptions, definition of oscillation, quantifier over solutions, spectral parameter, conclusion, or boundary cases. Selecting a familiar Sturm, nodal-count, spectral, comparison, or Kneser formulation would add proposition-changing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an accepted source must fix the independent-variable domain and endpoint convention, scalar or state space, equation and order, coefficient and spectral-parameter types, solution regularity, and every universe and typeclass assumption.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not say whether the result is an oscillatory/nonoscillatory classification, comparison implication, zero or nodal count, eigenvalue relation, sufficient or necessary criterion, asymptotic theorem, or another conclusion.
candidate_scope_not_credited: an equation on a half-line is oscillatory when a source-selected nontrivial solution has infinitely many or arbitrarily large zeros
all nontrivial solutions of a source-selected scalar second-order equation share an oscillatory classification
a Sturm comparison theorem transfers zero or oscillation behavior between two equations
a regular Sturm-Liouville eigenfunction has a source-specified nodal count
a coefficient condition such as a Kneser-type threshold implies oscillation or nonoscillation
a spectral counting result is equivalent to a zero count or relative oscillation index
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake because no proposition is selected; every zero-solution, degenerate-equation, domain, endpoint, repeated-zero, local-existence, singular-endpoint, threshold, and vacuity case must be resolved by the statement phase.
excluded_substitutions: THM-M-1384 Sturm-Liouville theory, THM-M-1385 Sturm comparison, THM-M-1386 Sturm separation, THM-M-1388 eigenvalue problems, or THM-M-1391 the Pruefer transform
